strings.name: Oliver Hart
strings.summary: Hart studies contracts that cannot specify every contingency, explaining how ownership and residual control affect investment and firm boundaries. Work with Grossman, Moore and others underpins incomplete-contract theory. He shared the 2016 economics Nobel with Holmström and continues research on contract design and corporate social responsibility.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Studies incomplete contracts and firm boundaries, providing frameworks for governance, privatization and property rights.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Cambridge mathematics BA (1969); Princeton economics PhD (1974).
strings.highlights.h1.title: Ownership and control
strings.highlights.h1.text: Explains how asset ownership shapes bargaining and investment when contracts are incomplete.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Theory and institutions
strings.highlights.h2.text: Applies property-rights analysis to integration, public services and corporate governance.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Cambridge honorary doctorate
strings.timeline.t1.text: His alma mater awarded an honorary science doctorate for economic and contract theory.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Shared economics Nobel
strings.timeline.t2.text: Won jointly with Bengt Holmström for contributions to contract theory.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Book on firms and contracts
strings.timeline.t3.text: Firms, Contracts, and Financial Structure examined ownership and financing arrangements.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Joined Harvard
strings.timeline.t4.text: Began a long appointment researching organizations, contracts and law and economics.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Foundational ownership paper
strings.timeline.t5.text: With Sanford Grossman, analyzed the costs and benefits of ownership.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Visiting appointment at MIT
strings.timeline.t6.text: Joined as visiting professor, becoming permanent the following year.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Doctorate and first lectureship
strings.timeline.t7.text: Earned Princeton’s doctorate and then lectured at Essex.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Completed mathematics degree
strings.timeline.t8.text: Graduated from King’s College, Cambridge, before moving into economics.
